slides.title:
The unusual part
is who makes the sauce.
slides.body:
Plenty of chefs cook modern Korean food. Far fewer make the fermented soy sauce it rests on. Kang told the Korea Economic Daily that after three years running a French restaurant he realised he had skipped past his own tradition, and went to Damyang to apprentice with a jang master rather than simply buy better sauce.

His reasoning was about attention rather than technique: the point, he said, is opening the jar regularly, turning it, watching it — that the process itself is what matters. It is a slow, unglamorous position for someone who trained in three of the most decorated kitchens in France.

What lands on the table is the result of that decision. Soy-marinated crab with black truffle reads as a stunt until you know the soy sauce was fermented by the person serving it.

caption:
A chef trained under Gagnaire, Robuchon and Ducasse now ferments his own soy sauce.

GiwaKang opened in Gangnam in December 2024 and took One MICHELIN Star in the Seoul & Busan 2026 guide. Lunch 220,000 won.

We haven't eaten here, and prices change.

Sources in the last slide.
